title: Story Time (Top 10 NH stories)
summary: A 3.5-hour stream where NH tells life stories: living in a mosque annex and a trap house as a US student, the worst day of his life in Paris, the forest 'black thing' sequel, his facial paralysis cured by his grandmother, school trips and near-death experiences. Between stories he answers free-for-all Q&A on programming, creatine, bulking appetite, lagging muscles, split squats, weight loss and self-improvement.
claims: Don't build a program from scratch early, but start tweaking your program from late novice/early intermediate once you know what your body likes; writing your own from scratch fits late intermediate/early advanced
One meal a day is not inherently bad for hypertrophy: total calories and macros matter, timing is secondary
He could never do OMAD because his single meal would need about 2,500 kcal, which he cannot stomach in one sitting
He has bulked 14 of his 15 years of lifting and done only one cut, which went badly, so he defers cutting advice to people who actually cut
Accept bad days: a day where nothing happens is the normal standard, happiness is a positive deviation; on hormonal 'blue days' just live through it and you feel better the next day
South Asian lifters have underrated bodybuilding genetics: often wide clavicles, big calves and legs, and shorter stature, so they mainly need to focus on upper body and back
Height doesn't matter in bodybuilding; 200 lb at 6'4 still looks wiry while 200 lb at 5'4 looks like a tank
Every time he trains with his gym buddy he PRs (a 10 lb PR on a long-trained compound that day), suggesting he pushes less hard alone at home than he thinks
Stop constantly changing programs; find one you like and stick to it
Ten sets of one exercise and one single set are both extremes; most people should sit somewhere in the middle on volume
To get sick less often, paradoxically expose yourself more to the elements and the cold
Creatine side effects vary: some report bloating, water retention or hair loss (DHT); he takes a tablespoon daily with no issues
Versus a barbell high pull, the power shrug is always the better trap choice
Very heavy trap overloading can hurt your neck; training the neck directly fixes that
If appetite limits your bulk, drink your calories: a heavy morning shake with ice cream, milk and almond or peanut butter, then find what else you can stomach
He dislikes adding an extra day for one lagging muscle: proper lower-body training grows glutes, and forearm isolation can simply go on upper days
He banned dumbbell split squats because at 75-80 lb for 12 he failed from balance, not leg fatigue; belt squat and safety-bar split squats let him load almost double

His Nigerian college roommate trained only 4 months a year, at most twice a week for 45 minutes, using a phone randomizer for exercises and reps, never to failure and never tracking, yet looked stage-ready and better than 95% of people: proof that genetics exist
He is certain that genetically gifted roommate was 100% natural
His cousin started benching and after two months had massive pecs, another example of elite genetics
For someone 12 kg overweight who stress-eats, fix the emotional overeating first, take a slow approach, and first master holding maintenance before cutting; yo-yoing 10 kg damages mental health
As a broke student making $700 a month he hid eggs and food in a mini fridge in his room because housemates stole them; he was bulked and quite fat at the time
He doesn't drink alcohol or eat pork simply by preference
At 10, cortisone treatment for facial paralysis made him gain 25 lb in one month, turning him from an athletic kid into a fat, depressed one
On a school trip to India he lost about 12 lb eating only rice, goat milk and sugar with almost no protein
The Paris fan-zone disaster taught him to stop people-pleasing: if he knows he won't enjoy something, he doesn't do it
Boasting about your achievements unprompted makes you look insecure
Respect and learn from him, but don't idolize him or anyone; he is just a regular guy
Changing environment is one of the only real ways to change yourself; studying abroad and living independently transformed him
Two weeks in grad school without speaking to anyone made him dissociate until his own name and face felt foreign; humans need social contact
A phantom queue at the Empire State Building showed herd mentality: a couple of people waiting made everyone wait, which is why masses are easy to manipulate
He tries to consume as little as possible and skips Black Friday
He was recently let go from a machine learning/AI job and thinks the AI bubble will pop soon
As a teen he ran uphill with a stray dog, which was humbling but good motivation
He does weighted carries and mace forearm work in his backyard
He lifts and does everything with glasses on
exercises: removes the balance limit of dumbbell split squats; 210 lb per leg
safety squat bar on back, sets of 12
banned: balance fails before legs at 75-80 lb
better than barbell high pull for traps; very heavy loads can strain the neck
no need for a separate forearm day
